comment: The revert-check of `documentation-ownership`'s route requirements (issues #13, #197, #712): one mutation per invariant — the resolution of a named skill path, the cost a row that routes a lettered sub-section must state, the ruler a section's cost is counted with, and the two forms a stated cost is compared in (a figure after a reference, and the range a row states as the span of the sections it names). Run it with `bash tools/mutate.sh --mutations tools/check-doc-routes-mutations.json`; `.pi/skills/mutation-runner` owns how, `.pi/skills/revert-check` owns the rule, and the CI step that owns the documentation routes prints `--list`, so a set that no longer parses fails the pipeline instead of rotting. `case-cmd` runs one named case (`--case {case}`), so a mutation pays one case and not the suite; the skill-path record names the case whose assertion it lands on, and that case asserts the same guard from three sides in its siblings (a path that no longer exists, a directory left without its `SKILL.md`, and a name that only prefixes an existing skill). The search is a single line and unique in its file, because the runner's replacement is literal and line-based, and the file is restored byte for byte afterwards.

mutations.label: skill-path
mutations.why: a documented skill path is resolved against the skills the tree carries, so a renamed or deleted skill fails the check instead of a run that needs it

mutations.label: route-states-its-cost
mutations.why: a row that routes a lettered sub-section states what those sections cost, so a row naming sub-sections and pricing nothing is reported instead of passing as routed

mutations.label: guideline-body-reference
mutations.why: a citation a guideline body writes is resolved beside the routing table's, so a split's parent number that stops being a heading fails the case when a body still cites it

mutations.label: section-cost-ruler
mutations.why: a section's cost is the byte count of its lines from the `## ` heading through the line before the next one, so a printed cost that is not that count fails the case

mutations.label: route-figure-is-measured
mutations.why: a figure a row writes after a lettered reference is that section's cost, so a row pricing a kilobyte of section at 0.1 kB is reported instead of passing as priced

mutations.label: route-range-is-the-span
mutations.why: a range a row states is the cheapest and the costliest of the lettered sections it names, so a range the measurement does not give is reported instead of passing as a span

mutations.label: companion-anchor
mutations.search: if ! awk -F'\t' -v f="$base" -v n="$num" '$1 == f && $2 == n { found = 1 } END { exit found ? 0 : 1 }' "$tmp/headings"; then
mutations.why: a companion's `## §N` anchor is resolved against its base document, so an anchor no section carries is reported instead of the companion becoming a document of its own

mutations.label: rule-name-one-document
mutations.search: { k = $1 SUBSEP $3; c[k]++; if (c[k] == 1) secs[k] = "§" $2; else if (c[k] == 2) secs[k] = secs[k] " and §" $2 }
mutations.why: one rule name stated twice in one document is the duplicate the one-normative-home rule forbids, so the name is counted per section and the second statement is reported

mutations.label: rule-name-two-documents
mutations.search: { k = $1 SUBSEP $3; if (!(k in seen)) { seen[k] = 1; docs[$3] = docs[$3] (docs[$3] == "" ? "" : ", ") $1 } }
mutations.why: two documents stating one rule name is the duplicate the one-normative-home rule forbids, found by the token the two statements share instead of by a reader's memory

mutations.label: rule-reference-resolves
mutations.search: if ! LC_ALL=C awk -F'\t' -v d="$doc" -v n="$num" -v nm="$name" '$1 == d && $2 == n && $3 == nm { found = 1 } END { exit found ? 0 : 1 }' "$tmp/rules"; then
mutations.why: a `see rule <File>.md §N "<name>"` reference is resolved against the rule names the section carries, so a renamed rule leaves its references reported with the names the section does carry

mutations.label: rule-with-no-name
mutations.search: if (!inrule) { p = index(line, "**Rule:"); if (p == 0) break; inrule = 1; line = substr(line, p + 7); name = "" }
mutations.replace: if (!inrule) { p = index(line, "**Rule: "); if (p == 0) break; inrule = 1; line = substr(line, p + 8); name = "" }
mutations.why: a rule with no name is reported with its file and line instead of being skipped by the extraction, so the empty case cannot pass as a rule the tree does not count
